<h1>Glossary</h1>
<p>Key terms used across the accelerometer course, with definitions that study teams can adapt to their own protocol, device, and analysis plan.</p>
<div class="lesson-meta">
<span>Terminology</span>
<span>QC variables</span>
<span>Study rules</span>
</div>
:::
:::

::: {.lesson-main}

::: {.glossary-grid}
<div><strong>Accelerometer</strong><p>A sensor that records acceleration over time, commonly along three axes.</p></div>
<div><strong>ActiLife</strong><p>ActiGraph desktop software used for device initialization, download, and selected conversion/review workflows.</p></div>
<div><strong>Bout</strong><p>A sustained interval classified within an intensity category under documented duration and bout-criterion rules. Current GGIR can calculate bouts in Parts 2 and 5.</p></div>
<div><strong>Calibration error (`calib_err`)</strong><p>Static calibration error after GGIR auto-calibration. Interpret it with `calib_status`, the QC report, the run configuration, and a pre-specified study rule rather than assuming a cutoff from the name alone.</p></div>
<div><strong>Cleaning code (`cleaningcode`)</strong><p>A GGIR sleep-output field used to understand cleaning decisions. Use the installed version's output documentation and the cleaned/full file distinction; do not delete numeric codes without a complete codebook and rationale.</p></div>
<div><strong>Clipping score (`clipping_score`)</strong><p>Fraction of 15-minute windows in a recording affected by clipping. The official GGIR output guide states that it should be zero; any non-zero value requires contextual review.</p></div>
<div><strong>Complete 24-hour cycle (`complete_24hcycle`)</strong><p>A recording-level completeness score: the fraction of 15-minute positions in the 24-hour cycle for which no valid data were available on any measurement day. It is not a Boolean day-completeness flag.</p></div>
<div><strong>Configuration (`config.csv`)</strong><p>The resolved GGIR parameter settings stored in the output directory. Archive it with the script and software versions because later runs may reuse values from it.</p></div>
<div><strong>Data dictionary</strong><p>A record linking each analysis variable to its source file, observation level, key, unit, GGIR configuration, transformation, missing-value rule, and decision status.</p></div>
<div><strong>ENMO</strong><p>Euclidean Norm Minus One; a raw-acceleration metric that summarizes dynamic acceleration after subtracting the static effect of gravity.</p></div>
<div><strong>Epoch</strong><p>A fixed time window, such as 5 seconds, used to summarize raw acceleration into counts or other aggregate values.</p></div>
<div><strong>`.agd`</strong><p>ActiGraph count-based data file; the course demonstration uses a 10-second epoch `.agd`, which is distinct from raw `.gt3x` data.</p></div>
<div><strong>`.gt3x`</strong><p>ActiGraph raw-data file commonly used as GGIR input.</p></div>
<div><strong>GGIR</strong><p>R package used to process raw accelerometer data into quality-control, activity, and sleep-related outputs.</p></div>
<div><strong>MET</strong><p>Metabolic equivalent; a unit used to express energy expenditure relative to rest.</p></div>
<div><strong>MVPA</strong><p>Moderate-to-vigorous physical activity.</p></div>
<div><strong>Non-wear</strong><p>A period when the device is likely not being worn by the participant.</p></div>
<div><strong>Observation level (grain)</strong><p>What one row represents, such as a recording, recording-day, recording-night, or participant. It determines the key and valid merge relationship.</p></div>
<div><strong>Pelotas/UFPel cohort example</strong><p>Course example used to illustrate real operations. It is not a universal rule set.</p></div>
<div><strong>QC</strong><p>Quality control; the process of reviewing logs, summaries, plots, and protocol rules to decide whether data are trustworthy.</p></div>
<div><strong>Raw data</strong><p>High-frequency sensor measurements before epoch aggregation or derived-outcome processing.</p></div>
<div><strong>Time window `MM` / `WW` / `OO`</strong><p>Part 5 windows running midnight-to-midnight, waking-to-waking, and sleep-onset-to-sleep-onset, respectively.</p></div>
<div><strong>Valid day</strong><p>A day that meets the study's minimum usable-data rule. In the course example: ≥10 hours awake wear and used as part of the ≥4 valid days plus ≥1 weekend day rule.</p></div>
<div><strong>Visual report (`visualreport`)</strong><p>The current per-recording GGIR Part 5 report (`report...`) designed to support QC. The optional legacy `old_report...` was not designed for data-quality assessment.</p></div>
<div><strong>Wear protocol</strong><p>The study's instructions for when, where, and how participants wear the device.</p></div>
:::
